_comment: Flood-article translation pipeline. Defaults are calibrated for an RTX 4060 Ti (16 GB, Windows/WDDM). See README.md 'Tuning' before changing the gpu section.

gpu._comment: Budget is in KV-cache slots = batch x (src_tokens + generated_tokens), NOT source tokens. One slot = decoder_layers*2*d_model*2 bytes = 96 KiB for the 1.3B, so peak_GiB ~= 2.56 + slots/10922. With autotune on, kv_slot_budget below is only a starting value: it is recomputed from target_peak_vram_gib and the checkpoint's real dims at load. max_batch_size is a fragmentation guard, not a throughput knob -- it caps the per-decode-step logits buffer (batch x 1.47 MiB).

generation._comment: max_new_token_* is the correctness cap handed to generate(): too low silently truncates translations, so it stays generous. budget_len_* is only used to reserve KV cache, and is tighter because KV grows lazily -- measured aggregate out/src ratio over 6,336 articles is 0.79, so reserving at 1.8 over-books batches ~2.3x. A batch that overshoots 1.25 just OOM-splits.

cpu._comment: block_size is a throughput knob, not just a memory one: a block is the pool from which same-language batches are formed, so bigger blocks mean fuller batches and fewer ragged tail batches per language. 26 cores / 512 GB RAM here, and a 6000-article block held ~112k chunks (~200 MB), so blocks are cheap: 24000 costs well under 1 GB of the ~430 GB free.
